newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Greenspan fails to spook most Asian forex dealers.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan fails to spook most Asian forex dealers.

text.p: Foreign exchange dealers in Asia reacted calmly on Thursday to Alan Greenspan's comment that the Federal Reserve may have to raise interest rates to head off a possible acceleration of inflation.
"It's more of the same. He's said most of this before," the head of foreign exchange trading at a European bank said.
Greenspant, the Fed chairman, told the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday; "It is conceivable...to have to move before you see evidence of real inflation emerging."
But the foreign exchange head said, "I interpret this to mean he isn't going to wait for the CPI (Consumer Price Index) to head up before he acts. We've known this all along."
Greenspan's comments prompted the dollar to jump nearly two pfennigs in New York to close at 1.6938 marks. It also rose more than one yen to end at 122.63 yen.
However, Asian players decided the New York market had perhaps over-reacted and were willing sellers at the higher levels. At 0305 gmt the dollar was quoted at 1.6900/05 marks and at 121.26/31 yen.
"Greenspan was honest about his intentions. He was stating the obvious and I don't see why the (New York) market reacted as it did," the director of trading at a European firm commented.
"Essentially he was saying 'if we see signs of increasing inflation, we'll put rates up to stop it.' Well, we've known that all along. The market reaction was overdone," he said.
The head of foreign exchange trading agreed. "The market has temporarily got ahead of itself. I'm still a bull on the dollar overall, but two pfennigs at a time is overdoing it," he said.

He said the dollar looked comfortable trading in a range of 120 to 125 yen and 1.66 to 1.71 marks. "The market will look for something really concrete before it breaks out of these ranges one way or the other," he said.

Kouichi Abe, a Manager at the Foreign Exchange Marketing Department of Nippon Credit Bank Ltd in Tokyo said the market was taken by surprise by the pre-emptive rate tightening aspect of Grennspan's testimony.
"But I don't think his comments were powerful enough to boost the dollar in Asia," Abe said, adding that technical factors appeared to be standing in the way of gains for now.
He said it is still hard to predict the direction of dollar/yen trade.

Asked if the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) was ready to tighten credit in March, Abe said, "It is possible. If Greenspan decides to hike rates, no one can complain after his warning yesterday."
But the manager of trading at an Australian bank in Singapore commented, "Perhaps he said it with a little more force this time, but what he did say wasn't new."
